lee (customer): getting lots of `invalid JSON` errors from streaming json mode when using our TS frontend + Go backend. happening intermittently. stack trace attached below :confused:

carmen (support): sorry about that — can you paste the exact error and the raw stream fragment? any repro steps?

lee (customer): error from our Go consumer: `json: unexpected EOF` on call to json.Decoder.Decode. Happens after ~10-30s of streaming. here's an extracted chunk from tcp dump (we sanitize keys):

```
{"event":"token","data":{"id":"abc123","role":"assistant","text":"Hel"
{"event":"heartbeat"}
{"event":"token","data":{"id":"abc123","role":"assistant","text":"lo world"}\n```

looks like `{"event":"token"...` got split and heartbeat framed in between.

carmen (support): thanks — which SDK versions and json_mode flags are you using? also are you using dedicated or private?

lee (customer): TS frontend uses `@redwood/sdk-js 0.5.2` with `json_mode: "json"` (streaming). backend is `redwood-go-client 0.4.9` using a bufio.Reader -> json.Decoder. Dedicated cluster in us-west. python workers also observed the same pattern but less frequent.

jon (eng-runtime): @carmen thanks for the tag. rough hypothesis: heartbeat frames are emitted as standalone NDJSON lines and the TS client is sending chunks without guaranteeing line boundaries, so the Go decoder sees mid-object fragments. can you confirm whether the TS client is doing any aggressive chunking/batching? :eyes:

carmen (support): @jon we asked customer — TS client uses Fetch stream with default chunk size, not doing explicit newline buffering.

sameer (eng-ml): this rings a bell. our streaming runtime interleaves control frames (heartbeat) as separate JSON lines. If a chunk boundary lands inside a JSON object, naive newline-splitting consumers can get broken objects. Some SDKs (python) have tolerant readers; Go's json.Decoder expects a full token.

jon (eng-runtime): repro plan: try reproducing locally with a small server that emits a large json token in two writes and a heartbeat write in-between. also test the TS SDK reading strategy — whether it emits `TextDecoder` chunk per fetch `ReadableStream` pull.

lee (customer): i can dump a minimal repro — attaching payload generator we used (sanitized):

```
async function emitStream(resp) {
  resp.write(JSON.stringify({event:'token', data:{text: 'A'.repeat(1024*8)}}));
  // simulate split
  await delay(10);
  resp.write('\n' + JSON.stringify({event:'heartbeat'}) + '\n');
  await delay(10);
  resp.write(JSON.stringify({event:'token', data:{text:'rest'}}) + '\n');
}
```

when Go reads with `dec := json.NewDecoder(bufio.NewReader(conn)); for dec.Decode(&m) {` it errors on the first decode.

jon (eng-runtime): thanks — that's sufficient. quick mitigation: in the Go consumer use a buffered scanner by newline or implement a small NDJSON tolerant loop: read bytes until `\n` and then `json.Unmarshal`. also in TS we can change the SDK to ensure newline is appended after every control frame write, or the runtime can coalesce to avoid mid-object splits.

carmen (support): can you try a quick workaround, lee? change Go consumer to read lines and unmarshal per-line and report back.

lee (customer): tried switching to `bufio.NewScanner` + `json.Unmarshal(scanner.Bytes(), &m)`, that removes the crash. app continues streaming.

sameer (eng-ml): good — that's a workaround. long term: runtime should not emit control frames inside an in-flight JSON object or the SDK should present a framing guarantee. which side we fix depends on breakage surface.

jon (eng-runtime): plan from infra/runtime: 1) TS SDK patch to ensure any `event` writes end with `\n` and to buffer partial chunks until a newline is observed; 2) runtime change to avoid splitting object writes across writes where possible; 3) add integration test with interleaved heartbeat during large token frames. i'll open a ticket and PRs.

deploy-bot: Created issue INC-1234: "streaming json-mode: NDJSON chunk interleaving causes decoder failures in Go consumers" (priority P2) — https://redwood.internal/INC-1234 :white_check_mark:

jon (eng-runtime): @lee and @carmen i'll link the repro in the issue. estimated patch in next sprint. in meantime recommend Go customers parse NDJSON by line.

carmen (support): relaying to customer. thanks everyone. :v:

lee (customer): thanks — workaround is fine for now. please ping me when the fix is merged. :pray:
